title: Descant Recorder
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Creative Arts; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Each learner uses their own recorder. Holes and fingers are described in words on the phone.

skills.key_step: The child names the head joint (mouthpiece and window), the body joint (finger holes and thumb hole) and the foot joint.

floor.prerequisite: Names parts of a string instrument (Grade 3).
floor.question: Which part of a string instrument shakes to make the sound?

steps: Find the finger holes and the thumb hole.
contexts: putting a recorder together after cleaning

misconceptions.repair: Hold a recorder and point to the mouthpiece.

misconceptions.ask: Where are most of the finger holes?
misconceptions.repair: Name the joints while placing fingers.
Name them from top to bottom: head, middle, foot.

misconceptions.ask: What is the hole at the back of the recorder for?
misconceptions.repair: Hold the recorder; find which finger covers the back hole.

checks.question: Where do you blow on a recorder?
Which finger covers the back hole?

skills.key_step: The child cares for a recorder: own use only, wash with cool soapy water, dry in shade, keep in a case.

floor.question: Why do we wash hands before eating?

steps: Wash with cool water and dry in shade.

board.do: A friend asks to play your recorder.
Wait for "no, we do not share".

misconceptions.repair: Say: hot water can bend the plastic.

misconceptions.ask: Wanjiku wants to use Otieno's recorder. What first?

listen_for: In the sun on the desk
misconceptions.ask: Where should a recorder be kept?
misconceptions.repair: Show a bent recorder from heat.

misconceptions.ask: Where should a wet recorder dry?
misconceptions.repair: Explain that heat can bend plastic.

checks.question: Why should you not share a recorder?

skills.key_step: The child orders B, A, G from high to low: B covers thumb and one hole, A two, G three, all with the left hand.

floor.question: Is a whistle high or low?

board.do: Add one finger: higher or lower?

misconceptions.ask: Which note covers the most holes?
misconceptions.repair: Play B A G and watch the fingers go down.

misconceptions.ask: How many fingers (with the thumb) does A need?
misconceptions.repair: Make a chart: B one, A two, G three.

misconceptions.ask: Which is the right order from low to high?
Which hand plays B, A and G?
misconceptions.repair: Put the left hand on top, near the mouthpiece.

checks.question: Which note is lowest: B, A or G?
How many front holes for A?

skills.key_step: The child describes good technique: sit or stand tall, cover holes with finger pads, blow gently, tongue each note.

floor.question: What does "piano" or soft ask for?

steps: Use the soft pads of the fingers.

misconceptions.repair: Blow gently and hard and compare.

listen_for: With the tip of the finger
misconceptions.ask: How do you cover a hole?
misconceptions.repair: Press a pad and a tip on a hole and see the leak.

misconceptions.ask: How should you sit to play?
How do you start a note on the recorder?

checks.question: What part of the finger covers a hole?
What happens if you blow too hard?
